intent: The button that opens and closes its Combobox's popup, drawn as a chevron unless given children of its own.
typical_uses: The chevron button of a ComboboxInput, placed as a child of the field when the field's own is turned off

dont_use_when.situation: The chevron at the end of a single-line combobox field

instead.note: ComboboxInput already renders this trigger, named by its `toggleLabel`, unless `showTrigger` is false.

dont_use_when.situation: A button that runs an action rather than opening a list

invariants.text: Without children the button renders a chevron glyph; any children replace it.

combobox.module.css positions the button absolutely at the inline end of its nearest positioned ancestor, square at the small control size and vertically centred; inside ComboboxInput that ancestor is the field's wrapper, and while the field's clear button is mounted the same rule that hides the field's own trigger hides this one.

anti_patterns.dont: Render the default chevron with no `aria-label`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label` (or visible children); the chevron alone gives the button no accessible name

children.states: children is any React content, shown in place of the default chevron
children.because: `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, popupSide, listEmpty, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A named trigger in place of the field's own

bad.title: A trigger outside any Combobox
bad.why: The primitive's Trigger reads the nearest Combobox root's state through context and throws when there is none.

A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
